title: America and Britain Almost Went to War Over a Pig 🐖
description:
In 1859, an American farmer on San Juan Island shot a British company's pig. Within weeks, 461 US troops faced five British warships. Nobody fired a shot. The only casualty was the pig.

Sources: National Park Service, San Juan Island NHP "The Pig War"; Wikipedia "Pig War (1859)"; HistoryLink.org essay 5037.

title: Rats Got Sued in Court. And They Got a Lawyer 🐀
description:
In the early 1500s, rats near Autun, France, were reportedly put on trial for eating the barley. Their lawyer, Barthélemy de Chasseneuz, argued that one summons wasn't enough and that the town's cats made the trip unsafe. The case was reportedly thrown out.

Sources: E. P. Evans, "The Criminal Prosecution and Capital Punishment of Animals" (1906); Wikipedia "Barthélemy de Chasseneuz"; Sky HISTORY "8 famous animal trials"; Grunge; Discover Magazine.

Voice is synthetic.

title: London Stank So Bad, Parliament Had to Act (1858) 🤢
description:
Summer 1858: a heatwave cooked the sewage in the Thames, right outside Parliament. MPs soaked the curtains in chemicals, talked about leaving London, then rushed through a law for new sewers.

Sources: Wikipedia "Great Stink"; London Museum, "A very smelly summer in the city"; Historic UK, "London's Great Stink".

title: A Bear Served in the Army and Carried Ammo 🐻
description:
In 1942, Polish soldiers in Iran adopted a bear cub named Wojtek. He loved beer and wrestling, was listed as a soldier so he could sail to Italy, and reportedly carried artillery shell crates at Monte Cassino.

Sources: Wikipedia "Wojtek (bear)"; Imperial War Museums, War Memorials Register; British Library, "Wojtek the soldier bear from the Polish army".

title: A Man Sold a Country That Didn't Exist 🗺️
description:
In 1822, Gregor MacGregor sold London on "Poyais", a Central American country he invented, with a guidebook, banknotes and government bonds. About 250 settlers sailed there and found only jungle; more than half of them died. He was later tried for fraud in France, and acquitted.

Sources: Wikipedia "Gregor MacGregor"; Global Financial Data ("The Fraud of the Prince of Poyais"); Amusing Planet (2025); "Sketch of the Mosquito Shore" (1822).

Voice is synthetic.

title: 3 Men Got Thrown Out of a Castle Window and Survived 🪟
description:
Prague, 1618: angry nobles threw two royal governors and their secretary out of a castle window, about 70 feet up. All three lived. Catholics credited angels, later pamphlets claimed a pile of manure, and the secretary got a brand-new noble title.

Sources: Wikipedia "Defenestrations of Prague"; History Revealed, "The 1618 Defenestration of Prague explained".

title: In 1876, It Rained Meat in Kentucky 🥩
description:
On March 3, 1876, chunks of meat fell from a clear sky onto a farm in Bath County, Kentucky. Two men reportedly tasted it. The most popular explanation: a flock of vultures throwing up mid-flight.

Sources: Wikipedia "Kentucky meat shower"; The New York Times, March 10, 1876; Scientific American blog (Bec Crew, 2014); Mental Floss.

title: A Flower Once Cost More Than a House 🌷
description:
In the 1630s, Dutch traders paid fortunes for tulip bulbs that were still in the ground. One reportedly sold for 10,000 guilders. Then the market crashed. But was it really a disaster?

Sources: Wikipedia "Tulip mania"; Smithsonian Magazine, "There Never Was a Real Tulip Fever" (historian Anne Goldgar); Peter Garber's research (via Smithsonian).

title: His College Banned Dogs, So He Brought a Bear 🐻
description:
Lord Byron's college at Cambridge reportedly banned dogs. So around 1807 he got a tame bear, and said it should sit for a fellowship. Weird true history.

Sources: Byron's letter to Elizabeth Pigot (26 Oct 1807); Wikipedia "Lord Byron"; Far Out Magazine (2025); Mental Floss; Popular Science; The Wordsworth Trust blog.

title: Two Cities Went to War... and the Trophy Was a Bucket 🪣
description:
In 1325, little Modena beat Bologna's much bigger army, then reportedly grabbed a wooden bucket from a well by Bologna's gate as a trophy. Legend says the bucket started the war; it didn't, but Modena still has it.

Sources: Wikipedia "War of the Bucket" and "Battle of Zappolino" (EN + IT); City of Modena, Palazzo Comunale (UNESCO site pages); TheCollector, "The War of the Bucket".
